subtitle: How Monastery Gates Became Doors to Healing

panels.shot: twilight wide shot of a monastery gate on a dusty road, travelers gathered as a calm monk stands with a water bowl
panels.action: Buddhist Infirmary Keeper stands at the ancient monastery gate, holding a simple bowl of medicine as weary travelers and a shivering monk approach under the fading light of the road.

dialogue.text: In an age of wandering and war, Buddhist infirmary keepers turned quiet monasteries into shelters of care along the roads of India.

i18n.hi: भटकती उम्र और जंग के बीच, बौद्ध सेवादारों ने शांत मठों को राह के सहारा-घर बना दिया।

panels.shot: wide shot over the Magadhan hills near Rajagriha at dawn, smoke from cooking fires, winding paths with small wanderers
panels.action: The early sun rises over rocky hills near Rajagriha, winding paths dotted with tiny figures of wandering ascetics and traders threading through the dust.

dialogue.text: Fifth century BCE. Around Rajagriha, paths cut through rock and dust. Merchants, ascetics and messengers share the same hard road, and sickness walks beside them.

i18n.hi: पाँचवीं सदी ईसा-पूर्व। राजगृह के आसपास पत्थर और धूल के बीच पगडंडियाँ। व्यापारी, संन्यासी, दूत – सब एक ही कठिन राह पर, और बीमारी साथ चलती है।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of an early Buddhist vihara hall, monks seated as one elder recites, the infirmary keeper kneels listening intently
panels.action: Inside a simple vihara near Rajagriha, monks sit cross-legged as an elder reads from palm leaves; the Infirmary Keeper kneels near a doorway, face intent, hands folded.

dialogue.text: In the Vinaya, the Buddha’s monastic rules, care for the sick is not a kindness on the side. It is sewn into the discipline itself.

i18n.hi: विनय में, बुद्ध के संघ-नियमों में, रोगियों की सेवा कोई अतिरिक्त दया नहीं, अनुशासन की बुनियाद है।

panels.shot: close-up on the infirmary keeper’s face turned toward a sick monk lying on a mat, background blurred elder monk speaking
panels.action: The Infirmary Keeper turns from the recitation toward a frail monk on a reed mat, his brow furrowed, as the voice of the elder continues behind him.

dialogue.text: The Mahavagga of the Vinaya speaks plainly: whoever would serve the Teacher must also serve the sick. To ignore them is to break the path.

i18n.hi: विनय के महावग्ग में साफ कहा है: जो गुरु की सेवा करे, वह रोगी की भी करे; उन्हें छोड़ना मार्ग तोड़ना है।

panels.shot: medium shot of the infirmary keeper gently lifting a sick monk’s head, another monk passes a small bowl of ghee and oil
panels.action: In a shaded corner, the Infirmary Keeper props up a sweating monk, while another monk hands him a small clay bowl glistening with ghee and oil.

dialogue.text: So the rules list medicines as carefully as prayers: ghee, oils, decoctions, purgatives. The monk’s cell doubles as an infirmary, the bowl as both offering and remedy.

i18n.hi: तो नियम दवाओं को भी उतनी ही तसल्ली से गिनते हैं जितनी प्रार्थनाएँ: घी, तेल, क्वाथ, विरेचन। भिक्षु की कोठरी ही औषधालय, भिक्षा-पात्र ही नेवेद्य और दवा दोनों।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot from behind the infirmary keeper washing the sick monk’s feet in a basin, other monks watching with mixed emotions
panels.action: Kneeling, the Infirmary Keeper pours water over cracked feet into a clay basin, while two younger monks watch, one hesitant, one moved, in the dim hall.

dialogue.speaker: buddhist_infirmary_keepers
dialogue.text: “If we do not tend him,” he says softly, “who will walk the path?”

i18n.hi: “अगर हम इसे न संभालें,” वह हल्के से कहता है, “तो धर्म-मार्ग पर चलेगा कौन?”

panels.shot: wide shot showing different cells around a courtyard, in each small scenes: a monk mixing herbs, another fanning a patient, another fetching water
panels.action: Around an open courtyard, separate monk cells reveal small acts of care: one mixing herbs in a mortar, another fanning a dozing patient, a third walking in with a water pot.

dialogue.text: The Vinaya makes care a shared duty. Whoever can, nurses; whoever is ill, receives. The monastery slowly learns to breathe like a single body.

i18n.hi: विनय सेवा को साझा कर्तव्य बनाता है। जो सक्षम है, परिचर्या करता है; जो बीमार है, पाता है। मठ धीरे-धीरे एक ही शरीर की तरह साँस लेना सीखता है।

panels.shot: medium shot at the monastery gate, infirmary keeper speaking with a lay healer carrying a small basket of herbs
panels.action: At the gateway, the Infirmary Keeper stands in calm conversation with a lay healer, who carries a woven basket of roots and leaves slung over his shoulder.

dialogue.text: But monks are not locked away. The Vinaya also speaks of lay physicians, midwives, herb sellers. The monastery listens, trades knowledge, and remembers.

i18n.hi: पर भिक्षु दीवारों में क़ैद नहीं। विनय गृहस्थ वैद्य, दाई, वनस्पति-विक्रेताओं का भी ज़िक्र करता है। मठ सुनता है, ज्ञान बाँटता है, याद रखता है।

panels.shot: map-like bird’s-eye pulling up over the Ganga plain, dotted with small monastery complexes along trade routes, with faint lines linking them
panels.action: The view lifts over the wide Ganga plain, monsoon clouds above, small monastery roofs dotting the routes between Rajagriha and Pataliputra, linked by faint, glowing paths.

dialogue.text: Over the next centuries, monks and nuns carry these rules from vihara to vihara. A network grows, carrying not only doctrine but habits of care.

i18n.hi: आने वाली सदियों में भिक्षु-भिक्षुणियाँ ये नियम विहार से विहार ले जाते हैं। एक जाल बनता है, जो साथ में उपदेश और सेवा की आदतें भी ढोता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of a bustling early Pataliputra street, wooden houses, river in background, with a modest building open to the road
panels.action: A busy street in Pataliputra hums with carts and chatter, while one modest building stands open to the road, mats laid out inside, jars and water pots lined along a wall.

dialogue.text: Centuries pass. Empires rise and fall. By around 400 CE, a Chinese monk named Faxian walks these same plains, watching how this care has spread.

i18n.hi: सदियाँ बीतती हैं। साम्राज्य उठते-गिरते हैं। लगभग 400 ईस्वी में चीनी भिक्षु फाक्सियन इन्हीं मैदानों पर चलता है, देखता है सेवा कैसे फैल चुकी है।

panels.shot: interior wide of the charitable house, infirmary keeper tending to both a poor householder and a traveler, while a monk recites nearby
panels.action: Inside the open hall, the Infirmary Keeper adjusts a pillow under a gaunt householder while a dusty traveler sips warm broth; a monk sits nearby, murmuring verses.

dialogue.text: Faxian notes charitable houses in Pataliputra where the poor and travelers receive food, medicine, and rest. He writes from faith, yet he marks something new: care beyond the cloister.

i18n.hi: फाक्सियन पाटलिपुत्र की अनाथ-औषध-शालाएँ नोट करता है, जहाँ गरीब और पथिक को भोजन, दवा, विश्राम मिलता है। वह आस्था से लिखता है, पर नई चीज़ दर्ज करता है: मठ से बाहर तक फैली सेवा।

panels.shot: medium shot of the infirmary keeper examining a small palm-leaf register of patients while a lay official looks on
panels.action: The Infirmary Keeper runs his finger down a palm-leaf strip, lips moving as he counts names, while a lay official in simple cloth watches with interest.

dialogue.text: These are not hospitals in the modern sense. They are infirmaries and charitable houses, often simple halls where monks, officials and donors weave duty and compassion together.

i18n.hi: ये आज के अस्पताल नहीं। ये औषधालय और धर्मशालाएँ हैं, साधारण दालान जहाँ भिक्षु, कर्मचारी और दानदाता कर्तव्य और करुणा को साथ बुनते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of the infirmary keeper mixing a paste of herbs, ghee and oil in a stone mortar, shadows of patients behind
panels.action: Fingers steady, the Infirmary Keeper grinds herbs into ghee and oil in a stone mortar, the blurred outlines of resting bodies filling the background.

dialogue.text: Inside, practice is humble and practical: poultices, purgatives, baths, regulated diets. The Vinaya’s lists meet local plants and skills, and a shared medical memory takes root.

i18n.hi: अंदर की साधना सादी और कामचलाऊ है: पुल्टिस, विरेचन, स्नान, नियत आहार। विनय की सूचियाँ स्थानीय जड़ी-बूटियों और हुनर से मिलती हैं, और साझा चिकित्सीय यादें जमने लगती हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of the infirmary keeper sitting at night by a lamp with a visiting monk from another region, comparing palm-leaf texts
panels.action: By lamplight, the Infirmary Keeper and a travel-worn monk from another region sit cross-legged, placing their palm-leaf bundles side by side, comparing markings and gestures.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars like Kenneth Zysk and C. Pierce Salguero trace how such monastic meetings helped spread healing knowledge along pilgrimage routes, across regions and generations.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक विद्वान केनेथ ज़िस्क और सी. पियर्स साल्ग्वेरो दिखाते हैं कि ऐसे मठ-समागमों ने तीर्थ-पथों, प्रांतों और पीढ़ियों में औषध ज्ञान फैलाया।

panels.shot: wide shot of a different monastery along a forest road, a nun helping a sick woman at its gate, echoing the earlier scene
panels.action: Far away along a forest road, a nun in ochre robes steadies a sick woman at another monastery gate, mirroring the care once given within Rajagriha’s walls.

dialogue.text: From Magadha to the north-west, similar scenes unfold. Not every monastery opens its gate, not every pilgrim is received, but the pattern of care is no longer strange.

i18n.hi: मगध से उत्तर-पश्चिम तक, ऐसे ही दृश्य उभरते हैं। हर मठ द्वार नहीं खोलता, हर यात्री नहीं ठहरता, पर सेवा का ढर्रा अब अनसुना नहीं रहा।

panels.shot: low-angle shot outside the gate at dusk, infirmary keeper helping a weary traveler inside while other travelers watch, hesitant
panels.action: At dusk, the Infirmary Keeper supports a limping traveler through the gate, while two others, wary and tired, linger outside in the lengthening shadows.

dialogue.text: Every act of care forces a choice: who is allowed inside, who must remain at the gate, how far compassion extends beyond one’s own robe and rule.

i18n.hi: हर सेवा का काम एक चुनाव है: किसे अंदर जगह मिले, कौन द्वार पर ही रुक जाए, करुणा वस्त्र और नियम के पार कहाँ तक जाए।

panels.shot: close-up on the infirmary keeper’s hands placing a simple water bowl just outside the threshold, offering it to an untouchable-looking laborer
panels.action: The Infirmary Keeper’s hands gently set a plain bowl of water just beyond the threshold, meeting the hesitant gaze of a dust-covered laborer standing outside.

dialogue.speaker: buddhist_infirmary_keepers
dialogue.text: “Sit,” he says quietly. “The rule is strict, but thirst need not be.”

i18n.hi: “बैठो,” वह धीमे से कहता है। “नियम सख़्त हैं, पर प्यास पर नहीं।”

panels.shot: wide shot showing both inside and outside the gate: patients resting within, travelers sheltered without under a tree, the infirmary keeper moving between
panels.action: The scene splits across the gate: inside, patients lie on mats in orderly rows; outside, travelers drowse under a tree; the Infirmary Keeper moves between, carrying a pot.

dialogue.text: The sources do not promise perfection. Faxian’s praise, the Vinaya’s ideals, the scholars’ reconstructions all hint at struggle: between law and need, between community and the stranger.

i18n.hi: स्रोत कोई परिपूर्णता नहीं बेचते। फाक्सियन की प्रशंसा, विनय के आदर्श, विद्वानों की रचना – सब संघर्ष की ओर इशारा करते हैं: नियम बनाम ज़रूरत, समाज बनाम अजनबी।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from an overhead view of the monastery gate by starlight, tiny lamp glowing where the infirmary keeper sits beside a patient
panels.action: Under a sky scattered with stars, the monastery lies quiet; near the open gate, a single lamp burns where the Infirmary Keeper watches over a sleeping patient.

dialogue.text: In these quiet infirmaries and roadside houses, a test was set that still stands: not how high a community builds its walls, but how it treats the sick who come to its gate.

i18n.hi: इन शांत औषधालयों और राह-किनारे धर्मशालाओं में एक कसौटी रखी गई, जो आज भी है: दीवारें कितनी ऊँची हैं नहीं, बीमार द्वार पर आए तो उनके साथ कैसा बर्ताव होता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: How Monastery Gates Became Doors to Healing
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे मठ-द्वार बने इलाज के दरवाज़े
